```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 5)
options(knitr.kable.NA = "")
```

The benchmark pipeline (`make benchmark`; `workflow/Snakefile`, `config/config.yaml`) prepares each dataset once, fits every method to the input it needs, and scores how well each method ranks proteins with a known change above unchanged ones. The tables and figures come from the files the pipeline exports to `inst/extdata`, so this page renders without data downloads.

- IonStar: E. coli spiked into a human background at five dilutions; quantified with MaxQuant, FragPipe and MetaMorpheus/FlashLFQ (with match-between-runs)
- CPTAC study 6: UPS1 spiked into yeast; MaxQuant
- ProteoBench DIA single-cell (Orbitrap Astral, 250 pg): yeast up fivefold against human; DIA-NN and MaxQuant
- ProteoBench DIA diaPASEF (timsTOF): E. coli up fourfold and yeast down twofold against human; DIA-NN and Spectronaut. The scores rank by signed statistics, so the fold change and t statistic of yeast are negated before ranking and both species count as changed
- Identification confidence (1 − PEP, or 1 − q-value for Spectronaut), which prolfqua's models use as weight, varies across samples in the ProteoBench and MetaMorpheus datasets; in the MaxQuant peptides.txt datasets it is one value per peptide; the FragPipe datasets carry none

- Ranking scores: fold change (`log_fc`), p-value signed by the fold change (`scaled.p_value`), t statistic (`t_statistic`)
- AUC, pAUC_5: area under the ROC curve, and partial area up to a false positive rate of 0.05, on a 0 to 100 scale, with all contrasts of a dataset pooled
- Contrasts computed: protein and contrast pairs with a result for the ranking score, all contrasts together. Each method is scored on the pairs it computes, so pAUC_5 is plotted against this count
- Pareto front (red): the methods no other method beats on both pAUC_5 and contrasts computed
- Same pairs: a method may be on the front because it tests fewer, easier proteins. The methods that test all its protein and contrast pairs (the same or more) are scored again on exactly these pairs (`same_pairs_scores()`; figure after the Pareto front, ranking by scaled p-value; `benchmark_same_pairs.tsv` has all three ranking scores)
- Front sets: the Pareto-front methods define sets of contrasts, sorted by size. Every method is scored on each set it computes completely (C2) and on the contrasts the next larger set adds (C3): are the extra contrasts of a method that computes more ranked well, or near random? (`front_set_scores()`; table and figure after the same-pairs figure, ranking by scaled p-value; `benchmark_front_sets.tsv` has all three ranking scores)
- Level: `protein` (model fitted to protein abundances), `peptide` (model fitted to peptides, one result per protein), `protein + peptide` (hurdle: intensity on proteins, detection on peptides)
- FDP vs FDR: the false discovery proportion at each nominal FDR; a calibrated FDR lies on the diagonal
- Calibration and power: the false discovery proportion against the number of true discoveries at a nominal FDR of 5%, one point per method, after the FDP vs FDR curves of each dataset
- Encoding: colour is the model family of the [prolfqua factory figure](https://github.com/fgcz/prolfqua#readme) (linear models, limma, limpa, LOD imputation, peptide level, hurdle); point shape and line type tell the models of a family apart; external tools are dark grey with open shapes. A method looks the same in every figure here and in the vignette `Score_history` (`method_scales()`, styles from prolfqua's `facade_styles.tsv`)

```{r read}
# The tables of the installed package: `make install` after `make benchmark`
extdata <- function(name, col_classes = NA) {
  path <- system.file("extdata", name, package = "prolfquabenchmark", mustWork = TRUE)
  utils::read.delim(path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, colClasses = col_classes)
}
scores <- extdata("benchmark_scores.tsv", col_classes = c(tool_version = "character"))
curves <- extdata("benchmark_curves.tsv")
methods <- extdata("benchmark_methods.tsv", col_classes = c(tool_version = "character"))
datasets <- extdata("benchmark_datasets.tsv")
preprocessing <- extdata("benchmark_preprocessing.tsv")
same_pairs <- extdata("benchmark_same_pairs.tsv")
front_sets <- extdata("benchmark_front_sets.tsv")
```

```{r method-style}
# Colour by model family, shape and line type by model within the family: the same in every figure of both vignettes
method_style <- function(method) {
  list(
    prolfquabenchmark::method_scales(method),
    ggplot2::theme_bw(),
    ggplot2::theme(legend.key.width = grid::unit(2.5, "lines"))
  )
}
# Prints a plot from inside the results = "asis" loop, in order with the text, with its own height and caption
print_with_height <- function(plot, height, caption) {
  header <- paste0(
    "```{r, fig.height = ", height, ", fig.cap = ", paste(deparse(caption, width.cutoff = 500L), collapse = ""), "}"
  )
  cat(knitr::knit_child(text = c(header, "print(plot)", "```"), envir = environment(), quiet = TRUE))
}
```

# Methods

```{r methods, results = "asis"}
methods_url <- "https://github.com/prolfqua/prolfquabenchmark/blob/main/inst/extdata/benchmark_methods.tsv"
methods |>
  dplyr::summarise(datasets = dplyr::n(), .by = c("method", "tool", "tool_version", "level", "input", "description")) |>
  dplyr::arrange(.data$tool != "prolfqua", .data$level, .data$method) |>
  dplyr::select("method", "tool_version", "level", "input", "datasets", "description") |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    escape = FALSE,
    table.attr = "class=\"table table-condensed\"",
    caption = paste0(
      "The ", dplyr::n_distinct(methods$method), " methods, with tool version, model level, the input the method ",
      "fits, the number of datasets it ran on (every dataset that provides its input, of ",
      dplyr::n_distinct(methods$dataset), ") and a short description. Per dataset and with the wall time of each ",
      "fit: <a href=\"", methods_url, "\">benchmark_methods.tsv</a>."
    )
  ) |>
  cat()
```

# Summary

```{r summary, results = "asis"}
summary_scores <- scores |>
  dplyr::filter(.data$contrast == "all", .data$score == "scaled.p_value") |>
  dplyr::select(method = "model_name", "dataset", "pAUC_5") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = "dataset", values_from = "pAUC_5") |>
  dplyr::select("method", dplyr::any_of(datasets$dataset))
summary_scores$median <- apply(summary_scores[, -1], 1, stats::median, na.rm = TRUE)
summary_scores |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(.data$median)) |>
  knitr::kable(
    digits = 1,
    format = "html",
    table.attr = "class=\"table table-condensed\"",
    caption = paste0(
      "pAUC_5 of every method on every dataset, ranking by p-value signed by the fold change (scaled.p_value), ",
      "all contrasts of a dataset pooled; empty where the dataset does not provide the method's input. Sorted by the ",
      "median over the datasets the method ran on. Each method is scored on the contrasts it computes; the dataset ",
      "sections below give the number of contrasts and the same-pairs comparison."
    )
  ) |>
  cat()
```

```{r datasets, results = "asis"}
for (dataset_name in datasets$dataset) {
  cat("\n\n# ", dataset_name, "\n\n", datasets$description[datasets$dataset == dataset_name], "\n\n", sep = "")
  cat(paste0("- ", preprocessing$step[preprocessing$dataset == dataset_name], "\n"), "\n", sep = "")
  dataset_scores <- dplyr::filter(scores, .data$dataset == dataset_name)
  positive <- datasets$positive[datasets$dataset == dataset_name]
  negative <- datasets$negative[datasets$dataset == dataset_name]
  n_contrasts <- length(setdiff(unique(dataset_scores$contrast), "all"))
  pooled <- if (n_contrasts == 1) "one contrast" else paste("all", n_contrasts, "contrasts pooled")
  pauc_5 <- dataset_scores |>
    dplyr::filter(.data$contrast == "all") |>
    dplyr::select("model_name", "score", "pAUC_5", contrasts = "n_total") |>
    dplyr::mutate(method = .data$model_name)
  front <- pauc_5 |>
    dplyr::filter(prolfquabenchmark::pareto_optimal(.data$pAUC_5, .data$contrasts), .by = "score") |>
    dplyr::arrange(.data$score, .data$pAUC_5)
  print_with_height(
    ggplot2::ggplot(pauc_5, ggplot2::aes(x = pAUC_5, y = contrasts, colour = method, shape = method)) +
      ggplot2::geom_step(data = front, ggplot2::aes(x = pAUC_5, y = contrasts), direction = "vh",
                         colour = "#e34948", linewidth = 1, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
      ggplot2::geom_point(size = 3) +
      ggrepel::geom_text_repel(
        ggplot2::aes(label = method),
        colour = "grey20",
        size = 3,
        segment.colour = "grey60",
        min.segment.length = 0,
        box.padding = 0.6,
        force = 6,
        max.overlaps = Inf,
        show.legend = FALSE,
        seed = 1
      ) +
      ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0.15, 0.4))) +
      ggplot2::facet_wrap(~score, ncol = 1) +
      ggplot2::labs(x = "pAUC_5 (all contrasts pooled)", y = "contrasts computed (protein and contrast pairs)",
                    title = paste(dataset_name, "pAUC_5 vs contrasts computed")) +
      method_style(pauc_5$method),
    height = 11,
    caption = paste0(
      "Ranking accuracy against the number of contrasts computed on ", dataset_name, ". Each point is one method. ",
      "x: pAUC_5, the partial area under the ROC curve up to a false positive rate of 0.05 (0 to 100), ", pooled,
      "; the ROC curve separates ", positive, " proteins (changed) from ", negative, " proteins (unchanged). ",
      "y: contrasts computed, the protein and contrast pairs with a result. Panels rank proteins by fold change (log_fc), ",
      "by p-value signed by the fold change (scaled.p_value) and by t statistic. Colour: model family as in the ",
      "prolfqua factory figure; shape: model within its family; grey open shapes: external tools. ",
      "The red staircase is the Pareto front: ",
      "no other method has both a higher pAUC_5 and more contrasts computed."
    )
  )
  dataset_same <- dplyr::filter(same_pairs, .data$dataset == dataset_name, .data$score == "scaled.p_value")
  if (nrow(dataset_same) > 0) {
    # one panel per set of contrasts, each with its own x axis; labels alternate above and below the line
    dataset_same <- dataset_same |>
      dplyr::mutate(panel = paste0(.data$front_method, ": ", .data$contrasts, " contrasts")) |>
      dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(.data$contrasts), .data$pAUC_5) |>
      dplyr::mutate(panel = factor(.data$panel, levels = unique(.data$panel)), y = 0) |>
      dplyr::mutate(label_y = ifelse(seq_along(.data$pAUC_5) %% 2 == 1, 0.55, -0.55), .by = "panel")
    lines <- dataset_same |>
      dplyr::summarize(from = min(.data$pAUC_5), to = max(.data$pAUC_5), .by = "panel")
    front_points <- dplyr::filter(dataset_same, .data$method == .data$front_method)
    print_with_height(
      ggplot2::ggplot(dataset_same, ggplot2::aes(x = pAUC_5, y = y, colour = method, shape = method)) +
        ggplot2::geom_segment(data = lines, ggplot2::aes(x = from, xend = to, y = 0, yend = 0),
                              colour = "grey40", linetype = "dashed", inherit.aes = FALSE) +
        ggplot2::geom_point(size = 3) +
        ggplot2::geom_point(data = front_points, ggplot2::aes(x = pAUC_5, y = y),
                            shape = 21, size = 5.5, stroke = 1.2, colour = "#e34948", inherit.aes = FALSE) +
        ggrepel::geom_text_repel(
          ggplot2::aes(label = method),
          nudge_y = dataset_same$label_y,
          direction = "x",
          colour = "grey20",
          size = 3,
          segment.colour = "grey60",
          min.segment.length = 0,
          max.overlaps = Inf,
          show.legend = FALSE,
          seed = 1
        ) +
        ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-1, 1), breaks = NULL) +
        ggplot2::facet_wrap(~panel, ncol = 1, scales = "free_x") +
        ggplot2::labs(x = "pAUC_5 on the panel's contrasts (all contrasts pooled)", y = NULL,
                      title = paste(dataset_name, "same contrasts, ranking by scaled.p_value")) +
        method_style(dataset_same$method),
      height = 1 + 1.6 * dplyr::n_distinct(dataset_same$panel),
      caption = paste0(
        "Ranking accuracy on the same contrasts on ", dataset_name, ", ranking by scaled p-value. Each panel is one ",
        "set of contrasts: those computed by a method on the Pareto front of the figure above (red circle), with their ",
        "number in the panel title. On the dashed line are the methods that compute all these contrasts, the same or ",
        "more, scored on these contrasts only (pAUC_5, ", pooled, "); each panel has its own x axis. A method to the ",
        "right of the red circle ranks these contrasts better: the front method's position then comes from computing ",
        "fewer, easier contrasts rather than from ranking them better."
      )
    )
  }
  # every method on each Pareto-front set (C1, C2) and on the contrasts the next set adds (C3)
  dataset_front <- front_sets |>
    dplyr::filter(.data$dataset == dataset_name, .data$score == "scaled.p_value") |>
    dplyr::arrange(factor(.data$method, levels = unique(.data$method)), .data$contrasts)
  dataset_front |>
    dplyr::select(
      Tool = "method",
      `C1 contrasts` = "contrasts",
      `C2 pAUC_5` = "pAUC_5",
      `Next C1` = "next_contrasts",
      Added = "added",
      `Added positives` = "added_positives",
      `C3 pAUC_5 of added` = "pAUC_5_added"
    ) |>
    knitr::kable(
      digits = 1,
      format = "html",
      table.attr = "class=\"table table-condensed\"",
      caption = paste0(
        "Every method on the sets of contrasts of the Pareto front on ", dataset_name, ", ranking by scaled p-value, ",
        pooled, ". C1: contrasts of the set, those a front method computes; C2: pAUC_5 of the method on the set; ",
        "Next C1: contrasts of the next larger set; Added: contrasts of the next set not in this one; Added ",
        "positives: ", positive, " (changed) pairs among them; C3: pAUC_5 of the method on the added contrasts. ",
        "Empty: the method does not compute all these contrasts. A random ranking has a pAUC_5 of about 2.5; C3 on ",
        "few added positives is not reliable."
      )
    ) |>
    cat()
  front_plot <- dplyr::bind_rows(
    dataset_front |>
      dplyr::transmute(
        .data$method,
        panel = "C2: pAUC_5 on the set",
        x = paste0(.data$contrasts, "\n", sub("^prolfqua_", "", .data$front_method)),
        order = .data$contrasts,
        y = .data$pAUC_5
      ),
    dataset_front |>
      dplyr::filter(!is.na(.data$next_contrasts)) |>
      dplyr::transmute(
        .data$method,
        panel = "C3: pAUC_5 on the contrasts the next set adds",
        x = paste0(.data$contrasts, " to ", .data$next_contrasts, "\n", .data$added_positives, " positives added"),
        order = .data$contrasts,
        y = .data$pAUC_5_added
      )
  )
  front_plot$x <- factor(front_plot$x, levels = unique(front_plot$x[order(front_plot$panel, front_plot$order)]))
  random <- data.frame(panel = "C3: pAUC_5 on the contrasts the next set adds", y = 2.5)
  print_with_height(
    ggplot2::ggplot(front_plot, ggplot2::aes(x = x, y = y, colour = method, shape = method, group = method)) +
      ggplot2::geom_hline(data = random, ggplot2::aes(yintercept = y), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
      ggplot2::geom_line(linewidth = 0.5) +
      ggplot2::geom_point(size = 3) +
      ggplot2::facet_wrap(~panel, ncol = 1, scales = "free") +
      ggplot2::labs(x = NULL, y = "pAUC_5", title = paste(dataset_name, "Pareto-front sets and the contrasts they add")) +
      method_style(front_plot$method),
    height = if (any(!is.na(dataset_front$next_contrasts))) 8 else 4.5,
    caption = paste0(
      "Every method on the sets of contrasts of the Pareto front on ", dataset_name, " (table above), ranking by ",
      "scaled p-value. Top: pAUC_5 on each set, labelled by its number of contrasts and the front method that ",
      "computes them, smallest first. Bottom: pAUC_5 on the contrasts the next larger set adds, labelled by the two ",
      "sets and the number of ", positive, " (changed) pairs among the added contrasts; the dashed line is a random ",
      "ranking. A method without a point does not compute all these contrasts. Colour, shape: method as in the ",
      "other figures."
    )
  )
  computed <- dataset_scores |>
    dplyr::filter(.data$contrast == "all", .data$score == "scaled.p_value") |>
    dplyr::select(model = "model_name", `contrasts computed` = "n_total")
  dataset_scores |>
    dplyr::filter(.data$contrast == "all") |>
    tidyr::pivot_longer(c("AUC", "pAUC_5"), names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") |>
    tidyr::unite("column", "metric", "score", sep = " / ") |>
    dplyr::select(model = "model_name", "level", "column", "value") |>
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = "column", values_from = "value", names_sort = TRUE) |>
    dplyr::left_join(computed, by = "model") |>
    dplyr::relocate("contrasts computed", .after = "level") |>
    dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(.data$`pAUC_5 / scaled.p_value`)) |>
    knitr::kable(
      digits = 1,
      format = "html",
      table.attr = "class=\"table table-condensed\"",
      caption = paste0(
        "Ranking scores on ", dataset_name, ", ", pooled, ", sorted by pAUC_5 of scaled.p_value. AUC is the ",
        "area under the ROC curve and pAUC_5 the partial area up to a false positive rate of 0.05, both on a 0 to ",
        "100 scale, for ranking by fold change, scaled p-value and t statistic. Contrasts computed: protein and ",
        "contrast pairs with a p-value."
      )
    ) |>
    cat()
  dataset_curves <- dplyr::filter(curves, .data$dataset == dataset_name)
  print_with_height(
    ggplot2::ggplot(dplyr::filter(dataset_curves, .data$curve == "ROC"),
                    ggplot2::aes(x = x, y = y, colour = method, linetype = method)) +
      ggplot2::geom_step() +
      ggplot2::coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 0.2)) +
      ggplot2::facet_wrap(~score) +
      ggplot2::labs(x = "false positive rate", y = "true positive rate", title = paste(dataset_name, "ROC")) +
      method_style(dataset_curves$method),
    height = 4.5,
    caption = paste0(
      "ROC curves on ", dataset_name, ", ", pooled, ". y: fraction of ", positive, " proteins (changed) ranked ",
      "above a threshold, the true positive rate; x: fraction of ", negative, " proteins (unchanged) above it, ",
      "the false positive rate, shown up to 0.2. One curve per method; panels rank by fold change, scaled ",
      "p-value and t statistic. Colour: model family as in the prolfqua factory figure; line type: model within its ",
      "family; grey: external tools."
    )
  )
  print_with_height(
    ggplot2::ggplot(dplyr::filter(dataset_curves, .data$curve == "FDP"),
                    ggplot2::aes(x = x, y = y, colour = method, linetype = method)) +
      ggplot2::geom_abline(colour = "grey60") +
      ggplot2::geom_step() +
      ggplot2::labs(x = "nominal FDR", y = "false discovery proportion", title = paste(dataset_name, "FDP vs FDR")) +
      method_style(dataset_curves$method),
    height = 4.5,
    caption = paste0(
      "Calibration of the FDR each method reports on ", dataset_name, ", ", pooled, ". x: nominal FDR threshold; ",
      "y: fraction of ", negative, " proteins (unchanged) among the proteins called significant at that ",
      "threshold, the false discovery proportion. One curve per method, colours and line types as in the ROC figure. A ",
      "calibrated FDR lies on the grey diagonal; curves above it are anti-conservative, with more false ",
      "discoveries than the FDR promises."
    )
  )
  at_fdr_5 <- dataset_curves |>
    dplyr::filter(.data$curve %in% c("FDP", "TP"), abs(.data$x - 0.05) < 1e-9) |>
    dplyr::select("method", "curve", "y") |>
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = "curve", values_from = "y")
  print_with_height(
    ggplot2::ggplot(at_fdr_5, ggplot2::aes(x = FDP, y = TP, colour = method, shape = method)) +
      ggplot2::annotate("rect", xmin = 0.05, xmax = Inf, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = "grey92") +
      ggplot2::geom_vline(xintercept = 0.05, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
      ggplot2::geom_point(size = 3) +
      ggrepel::geom_text_repel(
        ggplot2::aes(label = method),
        colour = "grey20",
        size = 3,
        segment.colour = "grey60",
        min.segment.length = 0,
        max.overlaps = Inf,
        show.legend = FALSE,
        seed = 1
      ) +
      ggplot2::expand_limits(x = 0) +
      ggplot2::labs(x = "false discovery proportion at nominal FDR 5%", y = "true discoveries at FDR 5%",
                    title = paste(dataset_name, "calibration and power at FDR 5%")) +
      method_style(at_fdr_5$method),
    height = 5,
    caption = paste0(
      "Calibration against power on ", dataset_name, " at a nominal FDR of 5%, ", pooled, ". Each point is one ",
      "method. x: false discovery proportion, the fraction of ", negative, " proteins (unchanged) among the ",
      "proteins with an adjusted p-value of 0.05 or less; right of the dashed line (grey area) a method calls more ",
      "false discoveries than the FDR promises. y: true discoveries, the ", positive, " proteins (changed) among ",
      "them. The best methods are top left. One threshold hides failures at a smaller FDR, which the FDP vs FDR ",
      "curves above show."
    )
  )
}
```
